svg.title: Computational modeling skills — research process
svg.desc: Planning, project setup, and literature guide the whole project. During investigation, model documentation records the hypothesis, lab records, and testing at the center. Modeling is at the top left, experimental analysis at the bottom left, theory at the top right, and simulations at the bottom right. Each remains a separate research activity. The last stage groups recording and notebook analysis, data visualization, claim-review, schematic design, and writing, with claim-review at its center. Thinking and reflection support personal growth through alignment and learning; scientific reproducibility supports external growth through the paper-reproduce skill. Arrows show exchange, evidence, or support rather than a mandatory execution sequence.

g.inkscape:label: Research process
g.text: Planning, setup and literature guide every stage

g.title: Research questions guide the literature search; evidence and gaps refine the research questions. Planning and literature are process steps here; the named cards are the fourteen included skills.
Model formulation, assumptions, and checks enter the research record; recorded hypotheses and testing guide model revisions.
Analytical predictions and their assumptions enter the research record; recorded hypotheses and tests guide theoretical analysis.
Recorded hypotheses and testing guide experimental analysis; methods, measurements, and observations return to the lab record.
Recorded hypotheses and testing guide simulations; settings, run records, and checks return to the model documentation.
Model predictions, analytical results, experimental measurements, simulation outputs, and their records contribute to results and analysis.
Recorded results and calculations support claim review; review findings may require further analysis or clearer records.
Plots support evidence review; review findings may require new comparisons or clearer visualizations.
Reviewed mechanisms inform schematics; schematics return to review for scientific fidelity.
Supported claims inform writing; drafted claims return to review against the evidence.
Alignment supports consequential choices throughout the research process.
Requested reflection supports learning from the research process.
Paper reproduction draws on whichever research activities the selected objective and target require.
Develop the research questions, focused directions, and precise problem statements in a cited, living research plan.
Project setup and repository rules organize the workspace and support every stage of the research process.
Find and assess primary sources; synthesize evidence and gaps to guide planning, investigation, interpretation, and writing.
Formulate a scientific model, compute its predictions, and check numerical and physical behavior.
Record the hypothesis, lab records, and testing, including model assumptions, equations, parameters, numerical methods, and sources.
Analyze stationary states and derive checked stability predictions and their limits.
Process experimental images and extract calibrated measurements for analysis and comparison.
Run authorized simulations on HPC resources, monitor execution, and record completed outputs.
Maintain a research record with calculations, code, observations, results, and interpretation.
Explore completed data and communicate quantitative results with clear comparisons and plots.
Assess claims against recorded calculations, results, plots, controls, and literature; return findings for revision.
Explain mechanisms and methods visually and assemble coherent scientific figures.
Develop an outline, draft, or revision from supported scientific findings.
Alignment: read context, expose gaps and assumptions, explain facts and tradeoffs, offer options and a recommendation, confirm unresolved choices, and deliver in the requested mode.
Learning: recap completed work, record agent rules and user lessons, suggest study topics, append dated lesson entries, and show the recap and saved files when explicitly requested.
External growth: learn from published research by reproducing, assessing, or applying a selected contribution.
